html:
Omar Bongo was president of Gabon for 41 years, from 1967 until his death in 2009, one of the longest rules of any modern head of state.

Born Albert-Bernard Bongo into a small Teke group in the southeast, he rose as an aide to Léon M'ba, who made him his successor. He made Gabon a one-party state in 1968, converted to Islam in 1973, and allowed rival parties again only in 1990.

He used oil money to buy loyalty across ethnic groups, which kept the country calm when its neighbours had wars. He was a central figure of Françafrique, close to every French president. His son Ali Bongo succeeded him, and the family's rule ended only with the coup of 2023.
sum: Omar Bongo was president of Gabon for 41 years, from 1967 until his death in 2009, one of the longest rules of any modern head of state.
